```{r setup, include=FALSE}
## Load targets results from other documents ----

tar_load(species_crosswalk)
tar_load(fvs_num_partitions)
tar_load(fvs_partition)

mgmt_ids <- c("NONE", "DFLT", "HVST", "SRVY", "BL56")
mgmt_methods <- tibble(
  mgmt_id = mgmt_ids,
  method = c("Projected", "Projected", "Projected", "Measured", "Projected")
)
mgmt_desc <- tibble(
  mgmt_id = mgmt_ids,
  desc = c(
    "Grow-Only",
    "Default",
    "Actual (Modeled)",
    "Actual",
    "1956 Baseline"
  )
)

for (mgmt_id in mgmt_ids) {
  f = list.files(pattern = paste0("*_CFICOP_", mgmt_id, ".Rmd"))
  normalizePath(f) |>
    tar_objects_defined_in_rmd() |>
    tar_load()
}

# Add a best estimate management ID

cficop_best_carbon <- cficop_none_bai |>
  select(StandID, Starting_Carbon, Projected_Carbon, Adjusted_AGLCF) |>
  group_by(StandID) |>
  summarize(
    Starting_Carbon = min(Starting_Carbon, na.rm = TRUE),
    Adjusted_AGLCF = mean(Adjusted_AGLCF, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  cross_join(
    tibble(Year = seq(1970, 2020, 10))
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Aboveground_Total_Live = Starting_Carbon + Adjusted_AGLCF * (Year - 1970)
  ) |>
  select(StandID, Year, Aboveground_Total_Live)

mgmt_ids <- append(mgmt_ids, "BEST")
mgmt_methods[nrow(mgmt_methods) + 1, ] <- list("BEST", "Projected")
mgmt_desc[nrow(mgmt_desc) + 1, ] <- list("BEST", "Grow-only, best estimate")
```

# Carbon on the Landscape

TODDO: this is probably not useful

-   Treat the 277 plots as a sample (by area?)
-   For the sample, we can compute the Standard Error of the Mean (SEM)
    as:
    -   SEM = s / sqrt(n) where s = sample standard deviation and n =
        number of points in the sample
    -   Note that if sample size \> 5% of the population size, also
        apply Finite Population Correction (FPC), which says
    -   SEM = s / sqrt(n) \* (N - n) / (N - 1) where N = population size
-   Then a 95% CI for the population mean is x_bar +/- (1.96 \* SEM)
    where x_bar is the sample mean

What does this mean for total carbon on the landscape?

I think we just multiply the FVS projected vs. corrected AGLCF times
years times acres (converted to hectares).

from above, estimated 56816 forested acres; we have 277 \* 0.2 = 55.4
acres, so 0.1%

## Summary Dataframe

CFICOP_NONE has the correct set of plots, e.g. it removes the plots
that don't have a sibling. Filter all management IDs to only those
plots.

Create the canonical dataframe of carbon.

```{r cficop_cmp_carbon, eval = FALSE}
cficop_nlyz_carbon <- lapply(mgmt_ids, \(mgmt_id) {
  get(paste0("cficop_", tolower(mgmt_id), "_carbon")) |>
    filter(Year %% 10 == 0) |>
    mutate(mgmt_id = !!mgmt_id) |>
    left_join(mgmt_methods, by = join_by(mgmt_id))
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  group_by(StandID) |>
  filter(any(mgmt_id == "NONE")) |>
  ungroup()

cficop_nlyz_carbon_summary <- cficop_nlyz_carbon |>
  rename(value = Aboveground_Total_Live) |>
  group_by(mgmt_id, Year, method) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    ymin = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE) - 1.96 * sd(value) / sqrt(n),
    ymax = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE) + 1.96 * sd(value) / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

# Graph It

```{r}
cficop_nlyz_carbon_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(Year, mean, color = mgmt_id)) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = method)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("Projected" = "dashed", "Measured" = "solid"),
    guide = guide_legend(order = 2)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(45, 150)) +
  labs(
    title = "Quabbin CFI Carbon Projection",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  xlab("Year") +
  ylab(bquote("Aboveground Live Carbon" ~(`Mg C` %.% ha^-1)))

```

# Bootstrapping

## NRS-18

NRS-18 says:

Using Forest Inventory and Analysis Data to Estimate Coefficient of
Variation and Number of Sampling Plots

* Download data (http://ncrs2.fs.fed.us/4801/fiadb/) and apply biomass equations
and expansion factors (see section 4.1) for the specific area and forest type of
interest. Sum to obtain plot level results.

* Calculate mean carbon stocks across the dataset or optionally across strata of
interest, then calculate standard deviation and the coefficient of variation.

* The minimum number of plots required for monitoring is calculated by solving
for n in the formula for the confidence interval (CI). Target ± 7 to 8 percent of the
mean as a reasonable level of precision (this accounts for the sampling error
only; sources of error such as measurement error and model error likely will
account for 10 to 20 percent of total error thus, a target of ± 7 to 8 percent CI
of the mean for sampling will result in a total error for the confidence interval of
about 10 percent of the mean).

$n = (s \times 2.1)/(mean \times 0.08)^2$

where s = standard deviation

let's look at mean and sd of carbon stocks in Quabbin in 1970:

```{r}
cficop_nlyz_carbon |>
  filter(mgmt_id == "SRVY") |>
  filter(Year == 1970) |>
  summarize(
    mean = mean(Aboveground_Total_Live),
    sd = sd(Aboveground_Total_Live)
  )
```

Mean is 51.14, sd is 21.24.

```{r}
(21.24 * 2.1)/(51.14 * 0.08)^2
```

which says 3 plots, which nobody is going to accept.

If the whole thing is squared:

```{r}
((21.24 * 2.1)/(51.14 * 0.08))^2
```

we get 119 plots, but this doesn't give 99 for CV=41.

Coefficient of variation is
([standard deviation * 100] / mean)

```{r}
((21.24 * 100) / 50)
```

42; in the sample table, Illinois has a CV of 41, for 99 plots.

NRS-18 also says that, for a 50-year projection, use "Large", which would
be 99 for Illinois, and 45 for Ohio.

## 100 Plots

What kinds of games could be played by selecting a subset of stands?

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# We can get a correlated sample by using a dataframe with all management IDs
tmp_carbon <- cficop_nlyz_carbon |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(StandID, Year),
    values_from = Aboveground_Total_Live,
    names_from = mgmt_id
  )

plot_carbon_100 <- lapply(1:10000, \(x) {
  tmp_stands <- tmp_carbon |>
    distinct(StandID) |>
    sample_n(size = 100, replace = FALSE)

  tmp_carbon |>
    semi_join(tmp_stands, by = join_by(StandID)) |>
    group_by(Year) |>
    summarize(
      NONE = mean(NONE),
      DFLT = mean(DFLT),
      HVST = mean(HVST),
      SRVY = mean(SRVY),
      BL56 = mean(BL56),
      BEST = mean(BEST)
    ) |>
    mutate(Sample = x)
}) |>
  do.call(rbind, args = _)

# Compute Percentile boostrap CIs
plot_carbon_100_ci <- plot_carbon_100 |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(mgmt_ids)) |>
  group_by(Year, name) |>
  summarize(
    lower_bound = min(value),
    lower_ci = quantile(value, probs = 0.025),
    middle_ci = quantile(value, probs = 0.5),
    upper_ci = quantile(value, probs = 0.975),
    upper_bound = max(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    dummy = "95% CI"
  )
```

# Population Mean

So, let's look at distribution of biomass in our 277 plot sample:

TODO: plot 10316 ends up with NA starting carbon and adjusted AGLF, why?

```{r population_mean, eval = FALSE}
hectares <- conv_unit(56816, "acre", "hectare")

population_mean <- cficop_none_carbon |>
  rename(
    Projected_Carbon = Aboveground_Total_Live
  ) |>
  left_join(
    cficop_none_bai |>
      select(StandID, Starting_Carbon, Projected_Carbon, Adjusted_AGLCF) |>
      group_by(StandID) |>
      summarize(
        Starting_Carbon = min(Starting_Carbon, na.rm = TRUE),
        Adjusted_AGLCF = mean(Adjusted_AGLCF, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "keep"
      ) |>
      ungroup(),
    by = join_by(StandID)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Adjusted_Carbon = Starting_Carbon + Adjusted_AGLCF * (Year - 1970)
  ) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarize(
    projected_carbon_mean = mean(Projected_Carbon, na.rm = TRUE),
    projected_carbon_sd = sd(Projected_Carbon), na.rm = TRUE,
    adjusted_carbon_mean = mean(Adjusted_Carbon, na.rm = TRUE),
    adjusted_carbon_sd = sd(Adjusted_Carbon, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "keep"
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    # convert sd to ci via 1.96 / sqrt(n)
    projected_carbon = projected_carbon_mean,
    projected_carbon_min = projected_carbon - projected_carbon_sd * 1.96 / sqrt(n),
    projected_carbon_max = projected_carbon + projected_carbon_sd * 1.96 / sqrt(n),
    adjusted_carbon = adjusted_carbon_mean,
    adjusted_carbon_min = adjusted_carbon - adjusted_carbon_sd * 1.96 / sqrt(n),
    adjusted_carbon_max = adjusted_carbon + adjusted_carbon_sd * 1.96 / sqrt(n)
  ) |>
  select(
    Year,
    projected_carbon, projected_carbon_min, projected_carbon_max,
    adjusted_carbon, adjusted_carbon_min, adjusted_carbon_max
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-Year) |>
  mutate(
    value = value * hectares,
    group = if_else(grepl("projected", name), "projected", "adjusted"),
    kind  = if_else(grepl("_min", name), "min", if_else(grepl("_max", name), "max", "mean"))
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("group", "Year"), names_from = "kind")
```

Plot it:

```{r plot population mean, eval = FALSE}
population_mean |>
  mutate(group = ordered(group, levels = c("projected", "adjusted"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(Year, mean)) +
  with_blur(
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = min, ymax = max, fill = group), alpha = 0.25),
    sigma = 3
    
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(color = group)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(order = 1),
    fill = guide_legend(order = 2)
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggtitle("Projected vs. Measured Total Carbon, 0.1% sample") +
  ylab(bquote("Total Carbon" ~(`Mg C`))) +
  scale_color_discrete(name = "Estimated\nPopulation\nMean") +
  scale_fill_discrete(name = "95% CI")
```

```{r population mean values, eval = FALSE}
population_mean |>
  filter(Year == 1970 | Year == 2020) |>
  mutate(ci = mean - min) |>
  select(group, Year, mean, ci)
```

In 1970, there were 1170155 +- 57272 Mg C / ha

In 2020, projected was 2839915 +- 80259

In 2020, adjusted was 2713476 +- 68425 2839915 - 2713476 = 126439,
126439 / 2839915 = 0.04452210718, so off by 4.5%

2713476 - 1170155 = 1543321 Mg C growth 126439 / 1543321 =
0.08192657263, so over-projects growth by 8%

## Calibrated vs Uncalibrated vs Observed

```{r, eval = FALSE}
for (max_scenario in 1:5) {
  plt <- cficop_cmp_carbon_summary |>
    filter(name %in% levels(name)[1:max_scenario]) |>
    filter(name != "Site Calibrated") |>
    ggplot(aes(Year, mean, color = name)) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = method)) +
    geom_point() +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name = "Scenario",
      values = c(
        "Default" = series_colors[1],
        "Site Calibrated" = series_colors[2],
        "Undisturbed (31)" = series_colors[3],
        "Best Estimate" = series_colors[4],
        "All Plots" = series_colors[5]
      ),
      guide = guide_legend(order = 1)
    ) +
    scale_linetype_manual(
      name = "Method",
      values = c("Projected" = "dashed", "Measured" = "solid"),
      guide = guide_legend(order = 2)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(48, 150)) +
    labs(
      title = "Projected vs. Measured Carbon"
    ) +
    xlab("Year") +
    ylab(bquote("Aboveground Live Carbon" ~(`Mg C` %.% ha^-1)))
  print(plt)
}
```

Q: Why does "Reference" go above Calibrated in this picture, but
originally it did not?

A: Because originally, we plotted the 31 plot Reference projection
against a 31 plot projection; now we have a 277 plot projection, and lo
and behold it is different!


How comparable are these?

```{r, eval = FALSE}
x <- cficop_none_carbon |>
  rename(Calibrated = Aboveground_Total_Live) |>
  left_join(
    cficop_dflt_carbon |>
      rename(Uncalibrated = Aboveground_Total_Live),
    by = join_by(StandID, Year)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    cficop_srvy_carbon |>
      rename(Measured = Aboveground_Total_Live),
    by = join_by(StandID, Year)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    cficop_none_bai |>
      select(StandID, Starting_Carbon, Projected_Carbon, Adjusted_AGLCF) |>
      group_by(StandID) |>
      summarize(
        Starting_Carbon = min(Starting_Carbon),
        Adjusted_AGLCF = mean(Adjusted_AGLCF),
        .groups = "keep"
      ) |>
      ungroup(),
    by = join_by(StandID)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Adjusted = Starting_Carbon + Adjusted_AGLCF * (Year - 1970)
  ) |>
  select(-c("Starting_Carbon", "Adjusted_AGLCF")) |>
  pivot_longer(-c("StandID", "Year")) |>
  union_all(
    cfigro_srvy_carbon |>
      select(StandID, Year, Reference = Aboveground_Total_Live) |>
      pivot_longer(-c("StandID", "Year"))
  ) |>
  filter(Year == 2020) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(StandID, Year))

t.test(x$Adjusted, x$Reference, paired=TRUE)
t.test(x$Uncalibrated, x$Adjusted, paired = TRUE)
t.test(x$Calibrated, x$Adjusted, paired = TRUE)
```

## Diameter Distribution

Look at distribution of trees by diameter class across time.

Treelists are big (millions of trees), so we don't hold on to the raw
list.

```{r dimater class distribution, eval = FALSE}
add_diameter_class <- function(x) {
  x |>
    mutate(diameter_class = case_when(
      DBH < 3 ~ 0,
      DBH < 5 ~ 3,
      DBH < 9 ~ 5,
      DBH < 15 ~ 9,
      DBH < 21 ~ 15,
      DBH < 40 ~ 21,
      .default = 40
    )
    )
}

fill_dbhlist <- function(x) {
  all_diameter_classes <- c(0, 3, 5, 9, 15, 21, 40)
  all_years <- unique(x$Year)
  all_stands <- unique(x$StandID)

  everything <- tibble(diameter_class = all_diameter_classes) |>
    cross_join(tibble(StandID = all_stands)) |>
    cross_join(tibble(Year = all_years))

  x |>
    full_join(everything, by = join_by(Year, diameter_class, StandID)) |>
    replace_na(list(tpa = 0))
}

cficop_none_dbhdist <- fvs_read_output(cficop_none, "FVS_TreeList") |>
  filter(Year %% 10 == 0) |>
  add_diameter_class() |>
  group_by(Year, diameter_class, StandID, random_seed) |>
  summarize(tpa = sum(TPA), .groups = "keep") |>
  group_by(Year, diameter_class, StandID) |>
  summarize(tpa = mean(tpa), .groups = "keep") |>
  ungroup() |>
  fill_dbhlist()

cficop_srvy_dbhdist <- fvs_read_output(cficop_srvy, "FVS_TreeList") |>
  filter(Year %% 10 == 0) |>
  add_diameter_class() |>
  group_by(Year, diameter_class, StandID, random_seed) |>
  summarize(tpa = sum(TPA), .groups = "keep") |>
  group_by(Year, diameter_class, StandID) |>
  summarize(tpa = mean(tpa), .groups = "keep") |>
  ungroup() |>
  fill_dbhlist()

cficop_dflt_dbhdist <- fvs_read_output(cficop_dflt, "FVS_TreeList") |>
  filter(Year %% 10 == 0) |>
  add_diameter_class() |>
  group_by(Year, diameter_class, StandID, random_seed) |>
  summarize(tpa = sum(TPA), .groups = "keep") |>
  group_by(Year, diameter_class, StandID) |>
  summarize(tpa = mean(tpa), .groups = "keep") |>
  ungroup() |>
  fill_dbhlist()

cfigro_srvy_dbhdist <- fvs_read_output(cfigro_none, "FVS_TreeList") |>
  filter(Year %% 10 == 0) |>
  add_diameter_class() |>
  group_by(Year, diameter_class, StandID, random_seed) |>
  summarize(tpa = sum(TPA), .groups = "keep") |>
  group_by(Year, diameter_class, StandID) |>
```

# Imaginary COP

We want two lines:
- Stored Carbon
- Baseline

For stored carbon, we also want bars
- Base of the bar is at the lag(1) stored carbon level
- Red bar for any growth in teh baseline
- Black bar for any growth in stored carbon - baseline
- top of the stacked bar should touch stored carbon here

## Simple

First, let's build sequences for stored carbon and baseline.

We can use the actual carbon summary for the modeled / observed,
but we need a baseline.

The 2.5%ile of the Monte Carlo for All Plots lands at about 74, whereas
the mean lands at about 98. Since actual management represents IFM already,
let's create a fake baseline by migrating from mean to the 2.5%ile over
50 years, which is subtracting 5 for each decade after 1970.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
imaginary_cop_baseline <- cficop_cmp_carbon_summary |>
  filter(name == "All Plots") |>
  mutate(
    name = "Baseline",
    mean = mean - 2 * (Year - 1970) / 10,
    ymin = ymin - 2 * (Year - 1970) / 10,
    ymax = ymax - 2 * (Year - 1970) / 10
  )
imaginary_cop <- cficop_cmp_carbon_summary |>
  union_all(imaginary_cop_baseline) |>
  mutate(
    name = ordered(
      name,
      levels = c(
        "Default", "Site Calibrated", "Undisturbed (31)",
        "Best Estimate", "All Plots", "Baseline"
      )
    )
  )
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
print(base_cop_plot)
```

## Years 1-9 Desk Reports

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# We need annual credit / debit.
credit_debit <- imaginary_cop |>
  filter(Year <= 1980) |>
  filter(name %in% c("Default", "Baseline")) |>
  # Create a table with a column per Year
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = "name", names_from = "Year", values_from = "mean"
  ) |>
  # Compute the annual accumulation for each
  mutate(
    starting_value = `1970`,
    annual_credits = (`1980` - `1970`) / 10
  ) |>
  distinct(name, starting_value, annual_credits) |>
  full_join(
    expand_grid(
      Year = 1971:1980,
      name = c("Default", "Baseline")
    ),
    by = join_by(name)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    value = starting_value + (Year - 1970) * annual_credits,
    credit_debit = if_else(name == "Baseline", "Debit", "Credit")
  )

total_credits <- credit_debit |>
  filter(credit_debit == "Credit") |>
  pull(annual_credits) |>
  sum()

total_debits <- credit_debit |>
  filter(credit_debit == "Debit") |>
  pull(annual_credits) |>
  sum()

credit_caption <- paste0(
  round((44/12) * total_credits),
  " Credits/ha - ",
  round((44/12) * total_debits),
  " Debits/ha = ",
  round((44/12) * total_credits - total_debits),
  " Credits/ha"
)

base_cop_plot +
  geom_rect(
    data = credit_debit |>
      filter(name == "Default" & Year < 1980),
    aes(
      xmin = Year - 0.2,
      xmax = Year,
      ymax = value,
      ymin = value - annual_credits,
      fill = credit_debit
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_rect(
    data = credit_debit |>
      filter(name == "Baseline" & Year < 1980),
    aes(
      xmin = Year,
      xmax = Year + 0.2,
      ymax = value,
      ymin = value - annual_credits,
      fill = credit_debit
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = imaginary_cop |>
      filter(name == "All Plots" & Year == 1970)
  ) +
  theme(
    aspect.ratio = 1,
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = -30, hjust = 0, vjust = 1)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1970, 1979), ylim = c(48, 75)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1970:1980) +
  labs(
    caption = credit_caption
  )

```

## Subsequent Re-Surveys

```{r, eval = FALSE}
credit_debit <- imaginary_cop |>
  filter(name %in% c("Default", "All Plots", "Baseline")) |>
  # Create a table with a column per Year
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = "Year", names_from = "name", values_from = "mean"
  ) |>
  arrange(Year) |>
  mutate(
    Baseline_Credits = Baseline - lag(Baseline),
    Baseline_Direction = if_else(Baseline_Credits > 0, "Debit", "Credit"),
    All_Plots_Credits = `All Plots` - lag(`All Plots`),
    All_Plots_Direction = if_else(All_Plots_Credits < 0, "Debit", "Credit"),
    Default_Credits = Default - lag(Default) - All_Plots_Credits,
    Default_Direction = "Reversal", 
  )

starting_credits <- credit_debit |>
  filter(Year == 1970) |>
  pull(`All Plots`)
ending_credits <- credit_debit |>
  filter(Year == 2020) |>
  pull(`All Plots`)
total_credits <- ending_credits - starting_credits

starting_debits <- credit_debit |>
  filter(Year == 1970) |>
  pull(Baseline)
ending_debits <- credit_debit |>
  filter(Year == 2020) |>
  pull(Baseline)
total_debits <- ending_debits - starting_debits

credit_caption <- paste0(
  round((44/12) * total_credits),
  " Credits/ha - ",
  round((44/12) * total_debits),
  " Debits/ha = ",
  round((44/12) * (total_credits - total_debits)),
  " Credits/ha"
)

base_cop_plot +
  geom_rect(
    data = credit_debit |>
      filter(Year > 1970),
    aes(
      xmin = Year - 1,
      xmax = Year,
      ymax = `All Plots`,
      ymin = `All Plots` - All_Plots_Credits,
      fill = All_Plots_Direction
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_rect(
    data = credit_debit |>
      filter(Year > 1970),
    aes(
      xmin = Year,
      xmax = Year + 1,
      ymax = Baseline,
      ymin = Baseline - Baseline_Credits,
      fill = Baseline_Direction
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_rect(
    data = credit_debit |>
      filter(Year > 1990),
    aes(
      xmin = Year,
      xmax = Year + 1,
      ymax = Default,
      ymin = Default - Default_Credits,
      fill = Default_Direction
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = imaginary_cop |>
      filter(name == "All Plots")
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = imaginary_cop |>
      filter(name == "All Plots")
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
additionality <- imaginary_cop_co2e |>
  filter(name == "Actual" | name == "Baseline") |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = Year, names_from = name, values_from = mean) |>
  mutate(
    direction = if_else(`Actual` < `Baseline`, "Emission", "Addition"),
    direction = factor(direction, levels = c("Addition", "Emission"))
  )

final_add <- additionality |>
  filter(Year == 2020) |>
  summarize(total = Actual - Baseline) |>
  pull(total) |>
  round()

imaginary_cop_co2e |>
#  filter(name %in% c("Actual", "Baseline")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = mean, color = name)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = additionality,
    mapping = aes(x = Year, ymin = Actual, ymax = Baseline, fill = direction, group = 1),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  # Add a ribbon outside the display
  # to keep "Emission" in the legend
  geom_ribbon(
    data = tibble(
      Year = c(1900, 1910),
      Actual = c(150, 200),
      Baseline = c(155, 205),
      direction = c("Emission", "Addition")
    ),
    mapping = aes(x = Year, ymin = Actual, ymax = Baseline, fill = direction, group = 1),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot_cop_style +
  annotate(
    "text",
    label = deparse("Additionality:"),
    parse = TRUE,
    x = 1990, y = 185,
    hjust = "left", vjust = "bottom"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    label = deparse(bquote(.(final_add) ~ Mg ~ CO[2]*e %.% ha^-1)),
    parse = TRUE,
    x = 2019, y = 155,
    hjust = "right", vjust = "bottom"
  )

```

# Alternate COPs

We created an imaginary baseline; now let's create 2 more imaginary
baselines and 2 more IFM scenarios

## imaginary_cops

Units are Mg CO2e ha^-1 yr-1

Create a High Harvest and Low Harvest scenario, each of which has
37Mg ha additionality.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
imaginary_cop_baseline2 <- imaginary_cop_co2e |>
  select(Year, name, mean) |>
  filter(name == "Actual") |>
  mutate(
    name = "Baseline 2",
    mean = mean - 100 * (Year - 1970) / 50
  )
imaginary_cop_ifm2 <- imaginary_cop_co2e |>
  select(Year, name, mean) |>
  filter(name == "Actual") |>
  mutate(
    name = "IFM 2",
    mean = mean - (100 - 37) * (Year - 1970) / 50
  )

imaginary_cop_baseline3 <- imaginary_cop_co2e |>
  select(Year, name, mean) |>
  filter(name == "Actual") |>
  mutate(
    name = "Baseline 3",
    mean = mean + 50 * (Year - 1970) / 50
  )

imaginary_cop_ifm3 <- imaginary_cop_co2e |>
  select(Year, name, mean) |>
  filter(name == "Actual") |>
  mutate(
    name = "IFM 3",
    mean = mean + (50 + 37) * (Year - 1970) / 50
  )

imaginary_cops <- imaginary_cop_co2e |>
  select(Year, name, mean) |>
  filter(name %in% c("Actual", "Baseline")) |>
  mutate(name = if_else(name == "Actual", "IFM", name)) |>
  union_all(imaginary_cop_baseline2) |>
  union_all(imaginary_cop_baseline3) |>
  union_all(imaginary_cop_ifm2) |>
  union_all(imaginary_cop_ifm3) |>
  mutate(
    name = ordered(
      name,
      levels = c(
        "IFM", "Baseline",
        "IFM 2", "Baseline 2",
        "IFM 3", "Baseline 3"
      )
    )
  )

imaginary_cops_addtly <- imaginary_cops |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = Year, names_from = "name", values_from = "mean")

ggplot_cops_style <- list(
  scale_color_discrete(
    name = NULL
  ),
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Scenario",
    values = c(
      "Actual" = "black",
      "High Harvest" = "darkred",
      "Low Harvest" = "royalblue"
    ),
    breaks = c(
      "Low Harvest",
      "Actual",
      "High Harvest"
    ),
    drop = FALSE
  ),
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1970, 2020), ylim = c(150,500)),
  scale_x_continuous(minor_breaks = NULL),
  ylab(expression(Mg ~ CO[2]*e %.% ha^-1)),
  theme_bw(base_size = 18),
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1),
  xlab(NULL)
)

imaginary_cops |>
  # The scenarios
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = mean, color = name)) +
  # Additionalities
  geom_ribbon(
    data = imaginary_cops_addtly,
    mapping = aes(x = Year, ymin = Baseline, ymax = IFM, fill = "Actual", group = 1),
    alpha = 0.5,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = imaginary_cops_addtly,
    mapping = aes(x = Year, ymin = `Baseline 2`, ymax = `IFM 2`, fill = "High Harvest", group = 2),
    alpha = 0.5,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = imaginary_cops_addtly,
    mapping = aes(x = Year, ymin = `Baseline 3`, ymax = `IFM 3`, fill = "Low Harvest", group = 3),
    alpha = 0.5,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  ggplot_cops_style

```

# Verra 5.0

## Baseline

### Sensitivity

NRS-18 says we need the sd / mean; how much do these vary by sample size?

```{r, eval = FALSE}
c1970_actual <- cficop_none_carbon |>
  filter(Year == 1970) |>
  select(Aboveground_Total_Live)

# We have 277 rows; let's start at sample size 20, and do 100 iterations
# at each sample size
bootstrap <- lapply(seq(35,265,5), \(sample_size) {
  lapply(1:100, \(n) {
    c1970_actual |>
      slice_sample(n = sample_size) |>
      summarize(
        sample_size = !!sample_size,
        mean = mean(Aboveground_Total_Live),
        sd = sd(Aboveground_Total_Live)
      )
  }) |>
    bind_rows()
}) |>
  bind_rows()
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bootstrap |>
  group_by(sample_size) |>
  summarize(
    val = mean(sd),
    range = sd(sd),
    ymax = val + range,
    ymin = val - range
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(sample_size, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax)) +
  geom_ribbon()
```

So, a lot.

What does this say for n?

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bootstrap <- bootstrap |>
  mutate(
    n = (sd * 2.1)/(mean * 0.08)^2 
  )
bootstrap |>
  group_by(sample_size) |>
  summarize(
    val = mean(n),
    range = sd(n),
    ymax = val + range,
    ymin = val - range
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(sample_size, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax)) +
  geom_ribbon()

```

I think what we learn from this is that the Quabbin plots are very uniform.

### USFS Ecosubsections

Finzi 2020 used 193 unharvested FIA plots in EPA ecoregions 58g and 59b

This is a little odd, since FIA references USFS Ecosubsections, which
are NOT the same as EPA ecoregions.

Harvard Forest is in USFS Ecosubsection 221Ah; 58g and 59b extend into
southern New Hampshire, which is USFS Ecosubsections M211Bd and 221Ai.
So I'll look at plots in those two ecoregions.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
usfs_ecosub <- terra::vect(file.path(
  "/vsizip",
  "data/raw/Ecosys_EcomapSubsections_2007.gdb.zip",
  "Ecosys_EcomapSubsections_2007.gdb"
)) |>
  # These come in EPSG:4269, which is a meters projection
  # for North America. Convert to lat/lon like everything else.
  # Note that EPSG:4269 is NAD83, whereas EPSG:4326 is WGS84,
  # so this re-projection is not meter accurate.
  terra::project(crs("epsg:4326"))
```

When did we get plots in each ecoregion of interest?
```{r, eval = FALSE}
fia_plots_filtered(fiadb, plots = NULL, filter = \(.data, con) {
  .data |>
    filter(ECOSUBCD %in% c("M211Bd", "221Ah")) |>
    group_by(STATECD, COUNTYCD, PLOT) |>
    filter(INVYR == min(INVYR, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    group_by(ECOSUBCD, INVYR) |>
    summarize(n = n(), .groups = "drop")
}) |>
  group_by(ECOSUBCD) |>
  mutate(n = cumsum(n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(INVYR, n, color = ECOSUBCD)) +
  geom_step() +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1970, 2020), ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  ggtitle("Number of FIA plots in Ecosub M211Bd and 221Ah") +
  ylab("Number of Plots") +
  xlab("Year")
```

## Massachusetts Timber History

https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/22951
> Northeastern Forest Experiment Station 1956. The Timber Resource in
> Massachusetts. Upper Darby, PA: U.S. Department of Agriculture,
> Forest Service, Northeastern Forest Experiment Station. 45 p.

This was done in collaboration with Harvard Forest; maybe the
materials that went into it were preserved?

p 1:
The forest survey recently completed in Massachusetts shows that the
state has 3.3 million acres of commercia1 forest land. This land
supports 2.7 billion board feet of timber, an average of 800 board feet
per acre. 

p 4:
In 1952, sawmills in Massachusetts produced
130,000,000 board feet of lumber, 85 percent of it
(110,000,000 board feet ) from sawlogs harvested in local
forests. More than l9,OOO,OOO board feet of sawlogs were
received at the mills from out-of-state sources. On the
other hand, about 4,000,000 board feet of Massachusetts sawlogs were shipped out of the state (table 1).

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ma_timber_1952 <- tribble(
  ~Species, ~thousand_board_feet, ~pct,
  "White and red pine", 59722, 53,
  "Hemlock", 17082, 15,
  "Spruce and fir", 6792, 6,
  "Other softwoods", 149, NA,
  "Oaks", 11231, 10,
  "Birch-beech-maple", 10059, 9,
  "Other hard hardwoods", 2153, 2,
  "Paper birch", 3210, 3,
  "Other soft hardwoods", 2638, 2
)
```

There are a total of 2.7 billion board feet; in 1952 113,036 thousand
board feet were cut.

Let's look at that as an annual fraction of harvest:
```{r, eval = FALSE}
(113036 * 1e3) / (2.7 * 1e9)
```

So, roughly 4.19% harvested per year.

On p iv, it's noted:
THE NET GROWTH of forest growing stock in 1952 was about 80,000,000 cubic
feet. The 1952 cut from growing stock was almost 26,000,000 cubic feet.
The great surplus growth was in the hardwoods.

p 12:
For sawtimber trees, the cut is much closer to growth. In terms of
sawtimber volume, the board-foot cut of softwoods is more than 90
percent of the net annual growth, but the board-foot cut of
hardwoods is only one-third of their growth.
